backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation halves). In a fixed 300s budget more optimizer steps usually help a small model. Keep all other hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**18

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (accumulation becomes 2 steps of 64x2048 tokens, or none if the sequence length makes it exact). Optionally scale MATRIX_LR by 0.85. Tests the small-batch, many-steps regime.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**17

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 so more of the budget is spent at peak LR. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.3

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 to test a longer decay phase.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR doesn't reach exactly zero. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to soften early instability, which may allow higher LRs.
backlog.title: Short warmup 3%

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 for the token embedding Adam group.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalars.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1 for Muon's cautious weight decay, since the short training run may be over-regularized.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Make Muon weight decay follow the LR multiplier schedule, so it is WEIGHT_DECAY * lr_multiplier(progress) instead of constant. It is applied each step in the optimizer update.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decayed to zero

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.99) for smoother second-moment estimates.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 with ASPECT_RATIO = 85 (model_dim rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM, i.e. 512 or 640). A smaller model gets more steps in 300s. Verify the dim is a multiple of 128.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-faster

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO = 51 so model_dim is about 512 (a multiple of 128). It checks whether depth beats width at this compute budget.
backlog.title: Depth 10 narrower

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to double the number of heads. Check that the attention kernel and rotary code support it.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSSSL" or equivalent, so fewer layers use full attention. This speeds up attention. The final layer must stay long.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL-lite: all short plus last long

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" to test whether full context everywhere beats the speed loss.
backlog.title: Window pattern all long

backlog.spec: If the model uses logit softcapping (e.g. 15 or 30), change the cap to 15. If it has none, add logits = 15*tanh(logits/15) before the loss in the forward pass.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with SwiGLU, using hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64 so the parameter count is matched. It needs a gate projection and Muon must cover the new matrix.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 MLP to SwiGLU

backlog.spec: Make sure the matmuls run in bf16 under autocast and that torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and cudnn.allow_tf32 are True. This only matters if not already set. It raises throughput and so the number of steps in 300s.
backlog.title: Disable torch.compile dynamic overhead: use bf16 autocast check

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum ramp (e.g. 0.85 to 0.95) so it reaches 0.95 in 100 steps instead of 300. If the ramp is time-based, scale it proportionally.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter

backlog.spec: Raise the final Muon momentum to 0.97 and keep the ramp the same.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.97 final

backlog.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz iteration count in Muon from 5 to 4 to save time per step. Keep the coefficients the same.
backlog.title: Muon NS steps 4

backlog.spec: If value embeddings are used on alternating layers, remove them from half of those layers, which saves parameters and memory. If they are not used, skip this. Evaluate whether the loss is unchanged.
backlog.title: Untied value-embedding off for alternating layers

backlog.spec: Initialize the attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights to zero, or scaled by 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) if they already aren't zero, so the residual stream starts as near-identity.
backlog.title: Init scale lower for output projections

backlog.spec: Add a small auxiliary loss, 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2), computed in the training forward pass only. It stabilizes the logits. Don't change the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Dropout-free token-level z-loss

backlog.spec: Change Muon's momentum anchor in train.py from the standard 0.3 to 0.96 to strengthen history accumulation, which often stabilizes smaller-batch training despite higher noise, potentially allowing higher effective learning rates.
backlog.title: Increase momentum decay anchor

backlog.spec: Replace WINDOW_PATTERN to 'SLSSID' (shifted with a distinct right-side signal) instead of focal slide patterns, as this can sometimes maximize local signal-to-noise ratio within the limited context provided by the 262K total batch.
backlog.title: Use inverted attention window pattern

backlog.spec: Replace the static DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64 with a dynamic get_dynamic_batch_size(step) function that uses a linear decay schedule based on training duration (normalized by 300s) ranging from 64 to 32. The harness will compute the average batch size for this epoch; the goal is to lower the Windows pattern to 2.0 (double bar size) and then reduce the window to 1.6 and 1.4 respectively.
backlog.title: Combine reduction and adaptive batch sizes

backlog.spec: Modify the token weight decay schedule in train.py to decay quadratically rather than linearly: w_decay_step = (n_steps + warmup_steps) * 0.5 - 1 / (warmup_steps - 1) * 0.5 * n_steps instead of the current linear decay. This creates a flatter plateau during early training.
backlog.title: Introduce cosine-squared loss schedule

backlog.spec: Add a per-layer momentum boost term in the optimizer step, scaling the momentum anchor by 1.0 + 0.1 * layer_id for non-output layers, which helps propagate gradients through deeper layers without overfitting to the final layer.
backlog.title: Layer-wise momentum boost

backlog.spec: Attempt to change attention windows to be exclusively forward ([51,51,51,51]) with a very small 2x block size (1,1,1,1) instead of the full sliding context, forcing the model to learn purely local signal without cross-frequentating.
backlog.title: Unidirectional attention slice

backlog.spec: Introduce an adaptive buffer size mechanism in train.py that uses the number of active timing intervals in the current window to dynamically scale down the window size by 0.9 per interval, starting from the original 64. This effectively creates a time-varying batch size.
backlog.title: Adaptive buffer size

backlog.spec: Insert a channel-wise dropout with p=0.05 in the HeadDim projection layer instead of the standard transformer dropout. This forces the model to learn more robust channel features, potentially improving generalization.
backlog.title: Add channel-wise dropout

backlog.spec: Change the hyperparameter scale_factor_range to [0.001, 0.1] and add a custom adaptive scaling factor using a logarithmic schedule instead of the original range. This allows the model to explore a wider range of scaling factors.
backlog.title: Optimize scaling factor range

backlog.spec: Replace the current warmpadding schedule with a linear scaling LR schedule: lr(t) = lr_0 * (1 + t / n_steps) for t in [0, n_steps], which increases the learning rate over the epoch rather than decreases it.
backlog.title: Linear scaling LR schedule

backlog.spec: Replace WARMUP_RATIO = 0.0 with WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 (3%) to introduce a brief warmup period, allowing the optimizer to start at a higher effective learning rate compared to the current immediate warmup, potentially accelerating early convergence.
backlog.title: Short Warmup Phase

backlog.spec: Change UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.004 to UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008 to increase the step size for the lm_head weights, exploring if a more aggressive update on the output projection helps refine the loss landscape.
backlog.title: Increase Unembedding Learning Rate

backlog.spec: Change DEPTH = 8 to DEPTH = 6 and set ASPECT_RATIO = 44 (calculated as TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE / 64 / 128 * 2 to fit within budget) to create a shallower but wider model (模拟试题 dims), testing if depth efficiency improves final val_bpb.

backlog.spec: Modify the training loop to use adaptive timestep selection for buffer sizes (implicit in the harness logic, specifically by reducing the stride or doubling the effective buffer to activate earlier and more aggressively for potential local minima search)
backlog.title: Adaptive Potential Buffer

backlog.spec: Modify the momentum schedule inside the training loop to apply an additional momentum decay factor or boost per specific layers if not explicitly present, or reduce the global momentum anchor to 0.9 to increase responsiveness in early layers and stabilize in later ones.
backlog.title: Layer-wise Momentum Boost

backlog.spec: Replace the sliding window pattern with a unidirectional slice where only the last half of the attention heads look left or use a fixed slice of the window that halves the effective context computation cost while maintaining coverage
backlog.title: Unidirectional Attention Slice

backlog.spec: Modify the loss line in the training loop to apply a cosine-squared weight to the current step's gradient, emphasizing recent gradients to potentially escape flat local minima.
backlog.title: Cosine-Squared Loss Schedule

backlog.spec: Introduce a Dropout layer with p=0.1 on the input channels before the first Linear layer to randomize the parameter space and encourage smoother features.
backlog.title: Channel-wise Dropout

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.95) to ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.95) to increase the first-term averaging of gradients, which might lead to faster convergence in the early stages.

memo:
Helped: only the batch-size cut. TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 gave 1.0981 (-0.0164), the incumbent. More optimizer steps in 300 s matter most.

Did not help: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.3 (+0.0006), WINDOW_PATTERN "L" (+0.0047), depth 10 (+0.0227), SwiGLU (+0.0023). Several runs scored better than the incumbent but were rejected: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 (1.0935), embedding LR 0.4 (1.0921/1.0856), Muon momentum 0.96 (1.0915/1.0878), MATRIX_LR 0.05 (1.0900/1.0917), decaying weight decay (1.0974). Their deltas are small and the replicates disagree, so noise is substantial. The incumbent has only 1 run.

Next: replicate the incumbent to measure noise. Try TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17. Then combine the small gains (WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, embedding LR 0.4, MATRIX_LR 0.05). Avoid bigger models and attention-window changes. Check train.py first, since slots 2 and 4 were aborted because it already had those settings.
